MIGRATION.md: # Migration from golden-mac

dotkit setup created this repository (~/.dotfiles) from the Mac golden-mac on YYYY-MM-DD. This file lists what it carried over and what needs your attention. Work through the list, then delete this file and commit.
Setup uninstalled nothing that was on the Mac; the Homebrew packages stay installed. A file in the way of a dotkit link is renamed to <name>.before-dotkit.
## Carried over
| What | Where |
| 3 Homebrew formulae | nix/brews.txt |
| 2 Homebrew casks | nix/casks.txt |
| 2 Homebrew taps | nix/taps.txt |
| 7 App Store apps | nix/mas.txt |
| 2 npm tools | config/mise.toml |
| 3 pipx tools | config/mise.toml |
| 1 cargo tool | config/mise.toml |
| 1 go tool | config/mise.toml |
| runtime versions of nvm, fnm, asdf, sdkman | config/mise.toml |
| 1 line of ~/.zshenv | config/zsh/zshenv (~/.zshenv.local) |
| 1 line of ~/.zprofile.local | config/zsh/zprofile (~/.zprofile.local) |
| 4 lines of ~/.zshrc | config/zsh/zshrc (~/.zshrc.local) |
| 1 line of ~/.bash_profile | config/bash/bash_profile (~/.bash_profile.local) |
| ~/.config/ghostty/config | config/ghostty.conf (~/.config/ghostty/config.local, read after the dotkit file) |
| ~/.config/starship.toml | config/starship.toml (instead of the dotkit file) |
| ~/.npmrc | config/npmrc (instead of the dotkit file) |
| ~/.config/git/config and ~/.gitconfig | config/gitconfig (~/.gitconfig, read after the dotkit file) |
| ~/.config/mise/config.toml | config/mise.toml |
| 4 other config files and directories | config/, linked with dotkit.links |
## To do
### Secrets

These lines have a secret, so they are not in Git. They are in a file in local/ of this repository, which Git ignores, and the repository file reads it. On a new Mac, copy the file by hand, or keep its lines in a manager for passwords.
- ~/.zshrc:22: `the function on this line, with a GitHub token` -> local/zshrc.zsh
### Logins
These files hold logins. They stay in place and are not in the repository.
- ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml: on a new Mac, `gh auth login`
- ~/.netrc: copy it by hand
### Config files
- config/ghostty.conf: Ghostty reads it after the dotkit settings. Delete the lines that you do not need to set again.
- config/starship.toml replaces the dotkit file config/starship.toml. Compare the two; the dotkit file has settings that yours does not, for example the Nerd Font symbols and the Git status.
- ~/.config/uv/uv.toml is replaced by the dotkit file and renamed to ~/.config/uv/uv.toml.before-dotkit. Copy the settings you miss to your own copy.
- config/npmrc replaces the dotkit file config/npmrc. Compare the two; the dotkit file has settings that yours does not, for example min-release-age=7 and prefix=${HOME}/.local.
- ~/.gemrc stays in place and outside the repository, because you chose to keep it. dotkit does not link its own file there. To get the dotkit settings, copy them from config/gemrc of dotkit.
- config/gitconfig: Git reads it after the dotkit settings (config/gitconfig of dotkit). Delete the settings that are the same. Your name and email are in ~/.gitconfig.user.

- ~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config: Ghostty reads it after ~/.config/ghostty/config, so it wins over the dotkit settings. Move its lines to config/ghostty.conf of this repository.

- ~/.config/ghostty is a link to ../dotfiles/ghostty. Setup renames the link to ~/.config/ghostty.before-dotkit before the first apply; the directory it points to stays, and these files of it are no longer at ~/.config/ghostty: themes/mine. Copy the ones you need into the repository.
- ~/.config/starship.toml is a link to ~/dotfiles/starship.toml. Setup renames the link to ~/.config/starship.toml.before-dotkit before the first apply; the file it points to stays.
### Shell lines: Done by dotkit
Nothing to do: the dotkit base sets this up (Homebrew, completion, fzf, zoxide, Starship, mise, direnv, suggestions, syntax colors).
- ~/.zprofile:1 `eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"`
- ~/.zprofile:2 `source ~/.zprofile.local`
- ~/.zshrc:29 `eval "$(starship init zsh)"`
- ~/.bash_profile:2 `[ -f ~/.bashrc ] && . ~/.bashrc`
### Shell lines: Conditionals and blocks
Copy the block to config/bash/bash_profile if you still need it.
- ~/.zprofile.local:2-4 `golden_broken() {` (+2 lines) (zsh -n could not check it)
### Shell lines: Shell framework
dotkit has completion, suggestions, syntax colors, and a prompt without a framework. Add the plugin lines you miss to config/zsh/zshrc. Remove the framework directory when you no longer need it.
- ~/.zshrc:2 `export ZSH="$HOME/.oh-my-zsh"`
- ~/.zshrc:3 `ZSH_THEME="robbyrussell"`
- ~/.zshrc:4 `plugins=(git docker)`
- ~/.zshrc:5 `source $ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh`
### Shell lines: Version manager
mise replaces it, see "Version managers" below. mise reads .nvmrc, .node-version, .python-version, and .ruby-version files, and always .tool-versions.
- ~/.zshrc:7 `export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.local/share/nvm"`
- ~/.zshrc:8 `[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"`
- ~/.zshrc:9 `export PYENV_ROOT="$HOME/.pyenv"`
- ~/.zshrc:10 `eval "$(pyenv init -)"`
- ~/.zshrc:11 `. "$HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh"`
- ~/.zshrc:12 `export SDKMAN_DIR="$HOME/.sdkman"`
- ~/.zshrc:13 `[[ -s "$HOME/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh" ]] && source "$HOME/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh"`
### Shell lines: Prompt

dotkit draws the prompt with Starship (~/.config/starship.toml). To keep your own prompt, set `dotkit.zsh.integrations.starship.enable = false;` in nix/shell.nix and add the lines to config/zsh/zshrc.
### Shell lines: Shell options and key bindings
dotkit sets its own options (nix/modules/zsh/lib/options.zsh in dotkit). Copy the ones you want to config/zsh/zshrc. The keymap is in nix/shell.nix.
- ~/.zshrc:15 `bindkey -v`
- ~/.zshrc:16 `setopt AUTO_CD`
### Shell lines: PATH changes
The directory does not exist, or the line replaces PATH. Add a directory you still need to config/zsh/zshrc as path=(/the/dir $path).
- ~/.zshrc:19 `export PATH="$HOME/missing/bin:$PATH"` (not carried: $HOME/missing/bin does not exist)
### Shell lines
- ~/.zshrc.local was not read by ~/.zshrc, so nothing of it is carried. dotkit links its own ~/.zshrc.local and renames yours to ~/.zshrc.local.before-dotkit. Copy what you need.
### Other shell files
- ~/.profile: bash -l no longer reads it, because dotkit links ~/.bash_profile. Copy what you need to config/bash/bash_profile and link it as ~/.bash_profile.local.
- ~/.zlogin: It stays in place, and zsh still reads it after the dotkit files. Check that it still works, or move its lines to config/zsh/zshrc.
### Shell frameworks
dotkit's zsh does not load them. Remove each one when you no longer need it.
- Oh My Zsh: `rm -rf ~/.oh-my-zsh`
- Powerlevel10k: `rm -rf ~/.p10k.zsh`
### Login shell
Your login shell is /bin/bash. dotkit makes the zsh of Nix the login shell, so the config of bash is not used in new terminals.
### Version managers

mise replaces them; dotkit's shell does not load them. The base has Node 24, Python 3.14, and Ruby 3.4. A project pins its own versions with `mise use` or a .nvmrc, .python-version, .ruby-version, or .tool-versions file.

- nvm (~/.local/share/nvm): node v20.11.0, v22.1.0 (default 22). config/mise.toml has these versions now. Then remove its lines from the shell files (the report lists them) and `rm -rf ~/.local/share/nvm`
- fnm (~/.local/share/fnm): node v21.7.0. config/mise.toml has these versions now. Then remove its lines from the shell files (the report lists them) and `rm -rf ~/.local/share/fnm`

- pyenv (~/.pyenv): python 3.11.8, 3.12.2 (default 3.12.2). config/mise.toml has python from your mise config already, so these versions were not added; `mise use -g python@<version>` for one you need. Then remove its lines from the shell files (the report lists them) and `rm -rf ~/.pyenv`

- asdf (~/.asdf): go 1.22.0; node 18.19.0 (default 18.19.0); ruby 3.3.0 (default 3.3.0). config/mise.toml has these versions now. Then remove its lines from the shell files (the report lists them) and `rm -rf ~/.asdf`

- sdkman (~/.sdkman): java 17.0.10-zulu, 21.0.2-tem (default 21.0.2-tem). dotkit has the Zulu 17 JDK (JAVA_HOME). For another JDK: `mise ls-remote java`, then `mise use -g java@<version>`. Then remove its lines from the shell files (the report lists them) and `rm -rf ~/.sdkman`
### Tools that moved to mise
mise installs these at the end of setup (`mise install`). The old copies stay, and they can come first in PATH. Remove each one when the mise copy works.
- `npm:eslint`, was 9.0.0 in ~/.npm-global. Old copy: `npm uninstall -g eslint`
- `npm:typescript`, was 5.4.0 in nvm v22.1.0. Old copy: `npm uninstall -g typescript`
- `pipx:black`, was 24.2.0 in pipx. Old copy: `pipx uninstall black`
- `pipx:datasette`, was installed in uv tool. Old copy: `uv tool uninstall datasette`. Note: with datasette-vega
- `pipx:httpie`, was installed in uv tool. Old copy: `uv tool uninstall httpie`
- `cargo:cargo-watch`, was 8.5.2 in cargo install. Old copy: `cargo uninstall cargo-watch`
- `go:github.com/rakyll/hey`, was v0.1.4 in ~/go/bin/hey. Old copy: `rm ~/go/bin/hey`. Note: the command hey
- mise needs go for these: `mise use -g go`.
### Tools that are not in mise
They stay where they are. To add one to config/mise.toml:
- `pnpm` (nvm v22.1.0): dotkit has no global pnpm; each project supplies its own, with mise or corepack. `npm uninstall -g pnpm` when you no longer need it.
- `mytool` (uv tool): installed from a URL or a directory. Add it to config/mise.toml by hand.
mise builds cargo tools from source, so they are off by default. They stay where they are. To add one to config/mise.toml:
- `mytool` (cargo install): installed from git+https://github.com/me/mytool#abc123. Add it to config/mise.toml by hand.
dotkit has these tools already, so they are not added.
- `bat` (cargo install): dotkit has bat (from Nix). Old copy: `cargo uninstall bat`
mise builds Go tools from source, so they are off by default. They stay where they are. To add one to config/mise.toml:
- `mystery` (~/go/bin/mystery): no Go module information. Add it to config/mise.toml by hand.
### mise
mise still reads these files. Move their tools to config/mise.toml.
- ~/.tool-versions
- ~/.config/mise/conf.d/work.toml

- config/mise.toml: `idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools` is now `["node", "python", "ruby", "rust"]`, dotkit's list and yours, because a list in your config replaces dotkit's (yours was `["rust"]`). Check it.
### Homebrew copies of dotkit tools
The dotkit base has these tools, so they are not in your lists. The Homebrew copy stays installed. Remove it when nothing else needs it; brew says when another formula depends on it.
- `ripgrep`: dotkit has ripgrep (dotkit, from Nix). `brew uninstall ripgrep`
- `node`: dotkit has node (dotkit, from mise). `brew uninstall node`
- `zsh`: dotkit has zsh (nix-darwin, the login shell). `brew uninstall zsh`
- `ghostty`: dotkit has ghostty (dotkit cask). `brew uninstall --cask ghostty`
- `font-jetbrains-mono`: dotkit has the JetBrains Mono font (nix-darwin). `brew uninstall --cask font-jetbrains-mono`
### Homebrew taps
These taps are not on GitHub, so the list has their URL. Check it.
- `acme/tools`: git@gitlab.com:acme/homebrew-tools.git

- `corp/tap`: its URL cannot go into nix/taps.txt (it has a space). Add it by hand to `homebrew.taps` in nix/darwin.nix as `{ name = "corp/tap"; clone_target = "https://git.example.com/homebrew tap.git"; }`.
Homebrew merged these taps into its own. Remove them.
- `homebrew/cask-fonts`: `brew untap homebrew/cask-fonts`
### App Store apps
- `Keynote` (ID 409183695): another app has this name, so nix/mas.txt lists it as `Keynote (409183695)`.
### Other config that stays out of the repository
These stay in place. They hold state, caches, or logins, so they are not for Git.
- ~/.config/gh: holds login tokens
- ~/.config/someapp: holds state or caches
- ~/.config/tokenapp: has a secret
